Марк Аврелий.name: Marcus Aurelius
Марк Аврелий.description: Roman Emperor of the Antonine dynasty, reigning from 161 to 180 AD, and one of the greatest Stoic philosophers in history. Born into a noble family, he received a brilliant education and was adopted by Emperor Antoninus Pius. Raised as a future ruler, he studied philosophy, rhetoric, and law. He became emperor at 40, combining the management of a vast empire with profound philosophical reflections. He led numerous wars on the empire's borders, especially against Germanic tribes and Parthians. His main philosophical work, "Meditations," is a personal diary written in Greek, reflecting on Stoic philosophy, duty, virtue, acceptance of fate, and emotional control. Marcus Aurelius practiced Stoic principles in daily life: self-discipline, humility, justice, and service to the common good. He is known as the "philosopher on the throne"—a rare example of a ruler who sought to live according to his principles despite immense power. His reign is considered a "golden age" for the Roman Empire, though he spent most of his time on military campaigns defending borders. He died in a military camp in Vindobona (modern Vienna), leaving a legacy as a wise ruler and profound thinker.

Александр Македонский.name: Alexander the Great
Александр Македонский.description: King of Macedonia and one of the greatest military commanders in history. Son of King Philip II and Queen Olympias, and a student of Aristotle. At age 20, he inherited the throne after his father's assassination. During his 13-year reign, he created a vast empire stretching from Greece to India, conquering the Persian Empire, Egypt, and reaching the borders of modern-day Pakistan. Famous for military victories at the battles of Granicus, Issus, and Gaugamela. He founded over 20 cities named Alexandria, the most famous being Alexandria in Egypt. Known for strategic genius, personal bravery (often leading charges himself), respect for conquered cultures, and a drive to unite East and West. He introduced the practice of cultural blending, encouraging marriages between Macedonians and Persians. His campaigns spread Hellenistic culture across the known world. He died at 32 in Babylon, likely from fever, though the exact cause remains a mystery. After his death, his empire fragmented, but his legacy—the Hellenistic world—endured for three centuries. Alexander became a legend in his own time and remains a symbol of military genius, ambition, and the quest for global dominion.

Альберт Эйнштейн.name: Albert Einstein
Альберт Эйнштейн.description: German-born theoretical physicist of Jewish descent, one of the founders of modern theoretical physics, and winner of the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics. Born in Ulm, Germany, to an engineer. He showed no exceptional abilities as a child and was late to start speaking. Graduated from the Zurich Polytechnic. Worked in the patent office in Bern, where in his spare time he developed revolutionary physical theories. In 1905, his "annus mirabilis," he published four papers that changed physics: the photoelectric effect, Brownian motion, special relativity, and the famous formula E=mc². In 1915, he completed the general theory of relativity, which overturned our understanding of space, time, and gravity. He predicted gravitational waves and light deflection. With the rise of the Nazis in 1933, he emigrated to the U.S., working at the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton. He actively opposed Nazism and wrote to President Roosevelt about the possibility of an atomic bomb (though he later regretted it). Known not only as a brilliant scientist but also as a pacifist, humanist, and advocate for civil rights and socialism. His image—disheveled hair, mustache, and gentle smile—became a symbol of genius. Einstein transformed our understanding of the universe and remains one of the most influential scientists in history.

Будда.name: Buddha
Будда.description: Spiritual teacher, founder of Buddhism, and one of the most influential figures in human history. Born into a royal family in Lumbini (modern-day Nepal) as Siddhartha. Raised in luxury, at age 29 he encountered suffering, sickness, old age, and death, prompting him to leave the palace in search of truth. After six years of asceticism and meditation, at age 35 he attained enlightenment (Bodhi) under the Bodhi tree in Bodh Gaya. He became known as the Buddha—"The Awakened One." For 45 years he traveled across India, preaching the Dharma (teachings) and founding the monastic Sangha. His teaching is based on the Four Noble Truths of suffering and the Eightfold Path to liberation. Buddha taught that all beings can reach enlightenment through morality, meditation, and wisdom. He emphasized personal experience over blind faith and the Middle Way between asceticism and sensual indulgence. He died at age 80, entering Parinirvana. His teachings spread throughout Asia, becoming one of the world's major religions with hundreds of millions of followers. Buddha remains a symbol of wisdom, compassion, and spiritual awakening.

Владимир Ленин.name: Vladimir Lenin
Владимир Ленин.description: Russian revolutionary, politician, Marxist theorist, and the founder and first leader of the Soviet state. Born in Simbirsk to a school inspector. The execution of his elder brother Alexander for an assassination attempt on the Tsar deeply influenced Vladimir's revolutionary views. Expelled from Kazan University for participating in student protests, he later passed law exams at St. Petersburg University. In 1895, he founded the League of Struggle for the Emancipation of the Working Class, was arrested, and exiled to Siberia. After exile, he emigrated, living in Switzerland, Germany, France, and England. He developed the theory of imperialism and authored numerous Marxist works. In 1917, following the February Revolution, he returned to Russia in a "sealed train" through Germany. He led the October Revolution and became Chairman of the Council of People's Commissars. During the Civil War, he implemented "War Communism" before introducing the NEP (New Economic Policy). He founded the Comintern to spread world revolution. A practical revolutionary, he combined theoretical work with organizational leadership. He died after a series of strokes; his body remains embalmed in the mausoleum on Red Square. Lenin remains one of the 20th century's most controversial figures: a liberator and builder of a new society to some, and a tyrant responsible for millions of victims to others.

Джордж Вашингтон.name: George Washington
Джордж Вашингтон.description: American statesman, the first President of the United States (1789-1797), commander-in-chief of the Continental Army during the Revolutionary War, and one of the Founding Fathers. Born in Virginia to a planter family, he was home-schooled, worked as a surveyor, and later inherited the Mount Vernon plantation. In his youth, he served in the Virginia militia, gaining military experience during the French and Indian War. In 1759, he married wealthy widow Martha Custis, becoming one of the colony's largest landowners. He was elected to the Virginia House of Burgesses. In 1775, the Continental Congress unanimously elected him commander-in-chief of the colonial army. For eight years, he led the war against superior British forces, demonstrating strategic patience, endurance, and the ability to inspire troops. Following victory in 1783, he voluntarily resigned his commission and returned to Mount Vernon—an unprecedented act for a military leader. In 1787, he presided over the Constitutional Convention. In 1789, he was unanimously elected the first U.S. President and re-elected in 1792. He established many precedents: the two-term limit, the title "Mr. President," and the cabinet system. In 1796, he declined a third term, setting a lasting tradition. He died at Mount Vernon. Washington became a symbol of republican virtue, integrity, service, and the voluntary surrender of power. His image on the dollar bill and the naming of the capital immortalized him as the "Father of His Country."

Гай Юлий Цезарь.name: Julius Caesar
Гай Юлий Цезарь.description: Roman general, politician, writer, and dictator, one of the most influential figures in the history of Ancient Rome. Born into a patrician family, he received an excellent education in Rome and Rhodes. He began his political career as a tribune and held various offices. He rose to fame as a military commander during the Gallic Wars (58-50 BC), conquering all of Gaul and leading two expeditions to Britain. He wrote "Commentaries on the Gallic War," a classic of Latin literature. In 49 BC, he crossed the Rubicon with the words "The die is cast," starting a civil war against Pompey and the Senate. He won battles at Pharsalus, Thapsus, and Munda, becoming the sole ruler of Rome. He implemented calendar reforms (the Julian calendar), expanded citizenship rights, and initiated construction projects. He was proclaimed dictator for life and granted the title "Imperator." On March 15, 44 BC, he was assassinated by a group of senators led by Brutus and Cassius, who feared the return of monarchy. His death led to a new civil war and the fall of the Roman Republic. Caesar remains a symbol of military genius, political cunning, and ambition.

Жанна д'Арк.name: Joan of Arc
Жанна д'Арк.description: National heroine of France, a peasant girl who became a military leader and symbol of French resistance during the Hundred Years' War. Born in Domrémy, Lorraine, to a peasant family. At 13, she began hearing the "voices" of saints (Michael, Catherine, Margaret) calling on her to free France from the English. At 17, dressed as a man, she traveled to meet the Dauphin Charles VII in Chinon and persuaded him to give her an army. She led the liberation of Orléans in 1429, a turning point in the war. She participated in Charles VII's coronation in Reims. Captured by the Burgundians, allies of the English, she was sold to the English and faced a church trial. Accused of heresy and witchcraft, she was convicted and burned at the stake in Rouen on May 30, 1431, at age 19. In 1456, she was posthumously retried and declared innocent, and in 1920 she was canonized by the Catholic Church. Joan of Arc became a symbol of patriotism, faith, and heroism, inspiring generations of French people and remaining one of the most famous women in history.

Иисус.name: Jesus
Иисус.description: The central figure of Christianity, a preacher, teacher, and Messiah whose teachings laid the foundation for one of the world's largest religions. Born in Bethlehem and raised in Nazareth, Galilee, in the family of Joseph the carpenter and Mary. Little is known of his childhood except for an episode in the temple at age 12. He began his public ministry around age 30, preaching in Galilee and Judea. His teachings included parables about the Kingdom of God, commandments to love God and neighbor, and a call to repentance and new life. He performed many miracles: healings, resurrections, walking on water, and turning water into wine. He gathered a group of 12 apostles. He entered Jerusalem as the Messiah and cleansed the temple of merchants. Betrayed by Judas Iscariot, he was arrested, tried, and sentenced to crucifixion by the Roman Procurator Pontius Pilate. Crucified on Calvary, he died and, according to Christian faith, rose on the third day. His life, death, and resurrection became the cornerstone of Christianity, changing the course of world history. Jesus remains one of the most influential figures in human history.

Иосиф Сталин.name: Joseph Stalin
Иосиф Сталин.description: Soviet statesman, political, and military leader, Generalissimo, and the leader of the USSR from the mid-1920s to 1953. Born in Gori, Georgia, to a shoemaker. He studied at the Tiflis Theological Seminary but was expelled for revolutionary activities. He joined the Bolsheviks, participated in the 1905 revolution, and was repeatedly arrested and exiled. After the October Revolution, he held various posts, becoming General Secretary of the CC CPSU in 1922. After Lenin's death in 1924, he gradually consolidated power in his own hands, eliminating political rivals like Trotsky, Zinoviev, and Kamenev. He carried out industrialization, agricultural collectivization, and the "Great Terror" of the 1930s. During the Great Patriotic War, he headed the State Defense Committee and coordinated military actions. After the war, he contributed to the creation of the socialist camp and initiated the Cold War. He died in 1953. His reign was characterized by mass repression and a cult of personality, but also by industrial development and victory in the war. Stalin remains one of the 20th century's most controversial figures.

Клеопатра.name: Cleopatra
Клеопатра.description: The last queen of the Ptolemaic Kingdom of Egypt and one of the most famous women in history. Born in Alexandria, she received a brilliant education and spoke many languages. In 51 BC, she became co-ruler with her brother Ptolemy XIII but was later exiled. She returned to power with the help of Julius Caesar, becoming his lover and bearing a son, Caesarion. After Caesar's death, she allied with Mark Antony, becoming his wife and bearing three children. Together with Antony, she opposed Octavian (the future Emperor Augustus) in a struggle for control of Rome. Following defeat at the Battle of Actium in 31 BC and Antony's suicide, Cleopatra took her own life, legend says, by the bite of a poisonous asp. Her death marked the end of Hellenistic Egypt and the beginning of Roman rule. Cleopatra is renowned for her beauty, intellect, education, diplomatic skill, and romantic ties to Rome's two greatest leaders. She remains a symbol of female power, seduction, and tragic fate.

Христофор Колумб.name: Christopher Columbus
Христофор Колумб.description: Italian explorer, admiral, viceroy, and governor of the Indies who opened the Americas to European exploration. Born in Genoa, Italy, to a family of weavers. He took to the sea at a young age, sailing the Mediterranean. He developed a plan to reach India by sailing west across the Atlantic, based on the principle of a spherical Earth. After years of effort, he secured support from the Spanish monarchs Ferdinand and Isabella. On August 3, 1492, he set sail from Palos with three ships (Santa Maria, Pinta, Niña) and 90 men. On October 12, 1492, he reached the island of San Salvador (Bahamas), discovering the "New World," though he believed he had reached Asia. He made three more voyages (1493, 1498, 1502), discovering Caribbean islands, Central, and South America. He founded the first European colonies in the Americas. He died in Valladolid, never knowing he had discovered a new continent. His voyages launched the Age of Discovery, the colonization of America, and the global exchange between the Old and New Worlds. Columbus remains a symbol of courage, adventure, and the era of exploration.

Леонардо да Винчи.name: Leonardo da Vinci
Леонардо да Винчи.description: Italian painter, scientist, engineer, inventor, anatomist, and thinker of the Renaissance, one of the greatest polymaths in human history. Born in Vinci, near Florence, as the illegitimate son of a notary. He apprenticed with Verrocchio in Florence, where he developed his artistic and technical skills. He worked in Milan, Florence, Rome, and France. He created world-renowned paintings: the "Mona Lisa," "The Last Supper," and "Virgin of the Rocks." He conducted extensive scientific research, studying anatomy (through dissection), physics, mechanics, hydraulics, botany, and geology. He produced thousands of drawings and notes in mirror writing, detailing inventions like flying machines, submarines, tanks, and clockwork mechanisms. He studied bird flight and designed bridges, canals, and military engines. His approach integrated art and science, observation and experimentation. He served as court engineer and painter to the Duke of Milan and later the French King Francis I. He died in France, leaving a vast legacy of unfinished projects and ideas that were centuries ahead of their time. Leonardo remains a symbol of universal genius and infinite curiosity.

Мартин Лютер Кинг-младший.name: Martin Luther King Jr.
Мартин Лютер Кинг-младший.description: American Baptist minister, activist, and leader in the civil rights movement, 1964 Nobel Peace Prize laureate. Born in Atlanta, Georgia, to a pastor's family. He earned a PhD in theology from Boston University. In 1955, he led the Montgomery bus boycott following Rosa Parks' arrest. He became a primary leader of the movement, founding the Southern Christian Leadership Conference (SCLC). He organized massive nonviolent protests: marches, sit-ins, and voting rights campaigns. He delivered his iconic "I Have a Dream" speech in 1963 during the March on Washington. He played a pivotal role in the passage of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and the Voting Rights Act of 1965. He also spoke against the Vietnam War and poverty. On April 4, 1968, he was assassinated in Memphis, Tennessee. His philosophy of nonviolence (Satyagraha), inspired by Gandhi, and his powerful oratory made him a symbol of the struggle for equality and justice. King remains one of the most revered figures in American history.

Наполеон Бонапарт.name: Napoleon Bonaparte
Наполеон Бонапарт.description: French military commander and statesman, Emperor of the French (1804-1814, 1815), and one of the greatest military strategists in history. Born in Corsica to a family of minor nobility. He trained at military schools in France and became an artillery officer. He rose to prominence during the siege of Toulon in 1793, advancing rapidly in rank. In 1796-1797, he led the brilliant Italian campaign, defeating the Austrians. In 1798-1799, he directed the Egyptian expedition. In 1799, he staged a coup (18 Brumaire), becoming First Consul, and in 1804, he proclaimed himself Emperor. He enacted significant administrative, legal (the Napoleonic Code), educational, and financial reforms. He waged numerous wars, creating a vast empire stretching from Spain to Russia. He was victorious at Austerlitz, Jena, and Wagram, but suffered major defeats in Russia (1812) and at Waterloo (1815). He abdicated twice and was exiled to the island of Saint Helena, where he died. Napoleon reshaped the political map of Europe, spread the ideals of the French Revolution, and built a modern administrative system. He remains a symbol of military genius, ambition, and the Romantic era.

Уинстон Черчилль.name: Winston Churchill
Уинстон Черчилль.description: British statesman, Prime Minister of the United Kingdom (1940-1945, 1951-1955), war correspondent, writer, and Nobel Prize laureate in Literature. Born into an aristocratic family, he was the son of Lord Randolph Churchill. He studied at Harrow and Sandhurst. He served in wars in India, Sudan, and South Africa. As a war correspondent, he authored numerous books. He began his political career in 1900, holding various ministerial posts. In 1940, at a critical moment in World War II, he became Prime Minister, leading a coalition government. His speeches, such as "Blood, toil, tears and sweat" and "We shall fight on the beaches," inspired the nation. He worked with Roosevelt and Stalin as part of the "Big Three." After the war, he warned of the "Iron Curtain" and the onset of the Cold War. Though he lost the 1945 election, he returned to power in 1951. He was known for his wit, love of cigars and brandy, stubbornness, and unwavering faith in Britain. He died in 1965. Churchill remains a symbol of leadership in times of crisis and one of the 20th century's greatest orators.

Чингисхан.name: Genghis Khan
Чингисхан.description: Founder and first Great Khan of the Mongol Empire, and one of history's greatest conquerors. Born into the family of a Mongol tribe leader, his childhood was marked by his father's murder, captivity, and poverty. He united the fragmented Mongol tribes, creating a powerful military organization. In 1206, he was proclaimed Genghis Khan—the "Universal Ruler." He established the Yassa code of law, reorganized the army using a decimal system, and enforced strict discipline. He launched conquests that overtook Northern China, Central Asia, Persia, and parts of Eastern Europe. His empire became the largest contiguous land empire in history. While known for brutality in warfare, he was also noted for religious tolerance, support of trade, and the creation of an efficient administrative system. He died during a campaign against the Tanguts. His empire was divided among his sons, but Mongol influence spread across vast territories. Genghis Khan remains a symbol of military genius and the creation of an empire.

Чарльз Дарвин.name: Charles Darwin
Чарльз Дарвин.description: English naturalist, geologist, and biologist, best known for his contributions to the science of evolution through natural selection. Born in Shrewsbury to a medical family. He studied medicine in Edinburgh and theology at Cambridge but became captivated by natural history. From 1831 to 1836, he embarked on a round-the-world voyage on the HMS Beagle, collecting a vast array of specimens and making observations that formed the basis of his theory. He studied the geology of the Galapagos Islands, the fauna and flora of South America, and fossils. In 1859, he published "On the Origin of Species," detailing natural selection as the mechanism of evolution. The theory explained life's diversity through common descent and adaptation to environmental conditions. It sparked fierce debate, contradicting religious views on creation. He later published "The Descent of Man" (1871), applying the theory to humans. Darwin was a modest, methodical scientist who carefully gathered evidence. His theory became the foundation of modern biology and changed the understanding of humanity's place in nature. He died in Downe, Kent. Darwin remains one of history's most influential scientists.

Винсент Ван Гог.name: Vincent van Gogh
Винсент Ван Гог.description: Dutch post-impressionist painter and one of the most famous and influential figures in Western art history. Born in Groot Zundert, Netherlands, to a pastor's family. He worked as an art dealer, teacher, and preacher among poor miners. In 1880, he decided to become an artist. He studied in Brussels, Antwerp, and Paris. He lived in poverty, supported by his brother Theo. He created over 2,000 works of art, including paintings, drawings, and sketches. He developed a unique style characterized by vibrant colors, expressive brushwork, and emotional intensity. His famous works include "The Starry Night," "Sunflowers," "Bedroom in Arles," and "The Night Café." In 1888, he moved to Arles, where he produced his finest works. Suffering from mental health issues, he famously cut off part of his ear in 1888 and spent time in psychiatric hospitals. On July 27, 1890, he shot himself in the chest and died two days later. He sold only one painting during his lifetime, but his work gained worldwide recognition after his death. Van Gogh became the symbol of the suffering genius, whose art reflects the depth of human emotion and the beauty of the world.

Уильям Шекспир.name: William Shakespeare
Уильям Шекспир.description: English poet, playwright, and actor, widely regarded as the greatest writer in the English language and one of the world's pre-eminent dramatists. Born in Stratford-upon-Avon to a glove-maker. He was educated at the local grammar school. At 18, he married Anne Hathaway and had three children. Around 1590, he moved to London and began a career as an actor and playwright. He became a shareholder in the Lord Chamberlain's Men theatrical company, later known as the King's Men. He wrote 37 plays, including tragedies ("Hamlet," "King Lear," "Macbeth," "Othello"), comedies ("A Midsummer Night's Dream," "Twelfth Night," "The Merchant of Venice"), and histories. He also composed 154 sonnets and several narrative poems. His works explore human nature, passion, power, love, jealousy, and ambition. He introduced thousands of new words and expressions to the English language. He died in Stratford and was buried in the local church. While authorship debates persist, his impact on literature, theater, and culture is undeniable. Shakespeare remains a symbol of genius and the ultimate master of the word.

Вольфганг Амадей Моцарт.name: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart
Вольфганг Амадей Моцарт.description: Austrian composer and musician, one of the greatest composers in history, a child prodigy and a genius of the Classical era. Born in Salzburg to Leopold Mozart, a composer and violinist. He began playing the harpsichord at age 3 and composing at age 5. At age 6, he and his sister Nannerl began concert tours across Europe, astounding royal courts with his talent. He met emperors, kings, and the Pope. He wrote over 600 pieces, including operas ("Don Giovanni," "The Magic Flute," "The Marriage of Figaro"), symphonies, concertos, chamber music, masses, and requiems. He worked at the court of the Archbishop of Salzburg and later in Vienna as a freelance musician. He married Constanze Weber and had six children, of whom two survived. Despite his brilliance, he lived with financial difficulties. He died at age 35 in Vienna, likely from rheumatic fever, leaving his "Requiem" unfinished. Mozart combined virtuosity, melody, emotional depth, and structural perfection. His music remains among the most performed and beloved in the world.

Зигмунд Фрейд.name: Sigmund Freud
Зигмунд Фрейд.description: Austrian neurologist and the founder of psychoanalysis, one of the most influential figures in the history of psychology and psychiatry. Born in Freiberg, Moravia (now the Czech Republic), to a Jewish family, he moved to Vienna at age 3, where he lived for most of his life. He studied medicine at the University of Vienna, specializing in neurology. He worked with Jean-Martin Charcot in Paris, studying hysteria and hypnosis. He developed the method of free association and dream analysis. In 1899, he published "The Interpretation of Dreams," the foundational work of psychoanalysis. He created a model of the psyche: the Id (unconscious), Ego (consciousness), and Superego (morality). He introduced concepts such as repression, sublimation, the Oedipus complex, libido, and Thanatos. He developed theories on childhood sexuality, the significance of the unconscious, and the role of dreams and slips of the tongue. He founded the International Psychoanalytical Association. His ideas influenced literature, art, anthropology, and sociology. In 1938, after the Anschluss of Austria, he emigrated to London. He died of jaw cancer. Freud remains a controversial but fundamental figure in understanding the human mind.

Исаак Ньютон.name: Isaac Newton
Исаак Ньютон.description: English mathematician, physicist, astronomer, alchemist, and philosopher, one of the greatest scientists in history. Born in Woolsthorpe, Lincolnshire, to a farming family. His father died before his birth, and he was raised by his grandmother. He studied at Cambridge University, where he became a professor of mathematics. In 1687, he published "Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica," one of the most significant works in science. He formulated the three laws of motion and the law of universal gravitation, explaining planetary motion and the falling apple. He co-developed calculus (simultaneously with Leibniz). He studied optics, prismatically decomposing white light into a spectrum, and invented the reflecting telescope. He discovered the binomial theorem and methods for numerical approximations. He served as Master of the Mint, reforming England's currency system, and was President of the Royal Society. He engaged in alchemy and theology, writing more on religion than on science. He was a secretive, solitary figure, often embroiled in disputes (e.g., with Hooke and Leibniz). He died in London and was buried in Westminster Abbey. Newton laid the foundations of classical mechanics and mathematics, fundamentally changing our understanding of the universe.

Карл Маркс.name: Karl Marx
Карл Маркс.description: German philosopher, economist, sociologist, political journalist, and revolutionary socialist, and the founder of Marxism. Born in Trier, Prussia, into a Jewish family that converted to Lutheranism. He studied law, philosophy, and history in Bonn and Berlin, earning a PhD in Jena. He worked as a journalist, editing the "Rheinische Zeitung." In 1843, he married Jenny von Westphalen and moved to Paris, then Brussels, and finally London. In 1848, together with Friedrich Engels, he wrote "The Communist Manifesto," the foundational document of the communist movement. His major work is "Das Kapital" (Volume 1, 1867), an analysis of the capitalist mode of production. He developed the theories of historical materialism, class struggle, surplus value, and labor alienation. He founded the First International (1864). He lived in poverty in London, supported by Engels. His ideas influenced the labor movement, socialist and communist parties, and 20th-century revolutions. He died in London and was buried in Highgate Cemetery. Marx remains one of the most influential and controversial figures in the history of thought.

Лев Толстой.name: Leo Tolstoy
Лев Толстой.description: Russian writer, thinker, moral philosopher, and social activist, widely considered one of the greatest authors in the history of world literature. Born in Yasnaya Polyana to an aristocratic family, he was orphaned early and raised by relatives. He studied at Kazan University but did not graduate. He served in the CRM War and on the Caucasus. In 1862, he married Sophia Behrs and had 13 children. He wrote the epic novels "War and Peace" (1869), a saga of Russia during the Napoleonic era, and "Anna Karenina" (1877), a novel of love and society. He also created numerous novellas, short stories, plays, and pedagogical and philosophical works. In the 1880s, he underwent a spiritual crisis, developing a doctrine of nonviolent resistance to evil, and became a critic of Church and State. He founded a school for peasant children and advocated for simple living, vegetarianism, and the renunciation of property. He was excommunicated from the Church in 1901. His ideas influenced Gandhi and the nonviolence movement. At 82, he secretly left Yasnaya Polyana and died at Astapovo station. Tolstoy remains a symbol of moral searching and humanism.

Людвиг ван Бетховен.name: Ludwig van Beethoven
Людвиг ван Бетховен.description: German composer, protagonist of music, a composer whose soul speaks through heroic struggle and the victory of the spirit over destiny. Born in Bonn into a musical family, he showed musical talent from a young age, studying with his father and other local musicians. In 1787, he visited Vienna, where he may have taken lessons from Mozart. He moved permanently to Vienna in 1792, becoming a student of Haydn. He quickly gained a reputation as a virtuoso pianist and composer. By the late 1790s, he began to lose his hearing, a tragedy that severely impacted his life but did not break his spirit. He composed 9 symphonies (including the famous Third 'Eroica', Fifth 'Fate', and Ninth with its choral finale), 5 piano concertos, 1 violin concerto, 32 piano sonatas (including 'Moonlight', 'Pathétique', and 'Appassionata'), the opera 'Fidelio', the 'Missa Solemnis', and numerous chamber works. His music is characterized by drama, emotional depth, innovation, and power. He died in Vienna in 1827. Beethoven remains a symbol of struggle against fate, strength of spirit, and genius, whose music continues to inspire millions.

Михаил Булгаков.name: Mikhail Bulgakov
Михаил Булгаков.description: Russian and Soviet writer, playwright, theater director, and actor, one of the greatest Russian writers of the 20th century. Born in Kyiv into the family of a professor at the Kyiv Theological Academy. He graduated from the medical faculty of Kyiv University and worked as a doctor during World War I and the Civil War. In 1921, he moved to Moscow and abandoned medicine for literature. He wrote satirical novellas: "Diaboliad," "The Fatal Eggs," and "Heart of a Dog." He created plays for the Moscow Art theater, including "The Days of the Turbins," "Zoya's Apartment," and "Flight." His masterpiece is the novel "The Master and Margarita" (1928-1940), which blends satire, fantasy, philosophy, and biblical motifs. The novel was only published in 1966-1967, 26 years after his death. He also wrote "The White Guard," "Theatrical Novel," and a biography of Molière. His works faced severe criticism and censorship in the USSR. He died in Moscow from a hereditary kidney disease. Bulgakov remains a master of satire, mysticism, and deep psychological insight, and a symbol of creative freedom under totalitarianism.

Михаил Ломоносов.name: Mikhail Lomonosov
Михаил Ломоносов.description: The first Russian scientist of worldwide significance, a polymath, physicist, chemist, astronomer, geologist, metallurgist, poet, philologist, artist, and historian. Born in the village of Mishaninskaya (now Lomonosovo), Arkhangelsk Governorate, into a peasant-maritime family. At age 19, he walked to Moscow with a caravan, pretending to be a nobleman's son to enter the Slavic Greek Latin Academy. He graduated and later studied at the St. Petersburg Academy and in Germany. Upon returning to Russia, he became a professor of chemistry at the Academy of Sciences. He established Russia's first chemistry laboratory, founded glass production, and developed technology for making colored glass and smalt. He formulated the law of conservation of mass, developed the corpuscular theory, and studied atmospheric electricity. He founded Moscow University (1755). He wrote odes, tragedies, and satires, and created the theory of "three styles" in Russian literature. He reformed the Russian language and created scientific terminology. He studied Russian history and wrote "Ancient Russian History." He died in St. Petersburg. Lomonosov became a symbol of the Russian Enlightenment and universal genius.

Пабло Пикассо.name: Pablo Picasso
Пабло Пикассо.description: Spanish and French painter, sculptor, printmaker, ceramicist, and designer, one of the greatest and most influential artists of the 20th century. Born in Málaga, Spain, into the family of an artist and drawing teacher. He showed exceptional talent from childhood, studying in Barcelona and Madrid. In 1900, he first visited Paris and moved there permanently in 1904. He went through several periods: the Blue Period (1901-1904) with its melancholic blue-toned paintings; the Rose Period (1904-1906) featuring lighter works with Harlequins; and the African Period (1907-1909) influenced by African art. In 1907, he created "Les Demoiselles d'Avignon," a painting that laid the groundwork for Cubism, a revolutionary movement where objects are depicted from multiple viewpoints simultaneously. Collaborating with Georges Braque, he developed Analytical and Synthetic Cubism. He created over 50,000 works, including paintings, sculptures, ceramics, and engravings. He painted the famous "Guernica" (1937), an anti-war masterpiece. He was a member of the Communist Party. He died in Mougins, France. Picasso fundamentally changed art, shattering traditional forms and creating new ways of seeing the world.

Сальвадор Дали.name: Salvador Dalí
Сальвадор Дали.description: Spanish artist and one of the most famous representatives of Surrealism, known for his technical skill, precise draftsmanship, and the striking and bizarre images in his work. Born in Figueres, Catalonia, into a notary's family. He studied at the Royal Academy of Fine Arts of San Fernando in Madrid, from which he was expelled for insubordination. In 1929, he joined the Surrealists in Paris and met his muse and wife, Gala (Elena Diakonova). He developed the "paranoiac-critical method," a way of creating images through delusional associations. He created iconic paintings: "The Persistence of Memory" (the melting clocks), "Dream Caused by the Flight of a Bee Around a Pomegranate a Second Before Awakening," "The Face of War," and "Christ of Saint John of the Cross." He worked in cinema with Luis Buñuel ("Un Chien Andalou") and collaborated with Walt Disney. He created sculptures, jewelry, theater sets, and book illustrations. Known for his eccentric behavior, mustache, and provocative statements. In the 1940s, he broke with the Surrealists and turned to classical themes and religious subjects. He lived in the USA before returning to Spain. He died in Figueres, where he established his Theater-Museum. Dalí remains a symbol of Surrealism and a master of dreamlike imagery.

Сократ.name: Socrates
Сократ.description: Classical Greek philosopher from Athens, one of the founders of Western philosophy, and the teacher of Plato. Born in Athens, the son of the sculptor Sophroniscus and the midwife Phaenarete. He served in the Peloponnesian War, demonstrating bravery. He left no written works; his teachings are known primarily through the dialogues of Plato and Xenophon. He developed the Socratic method of dialogue and questioning (maieutics, or "midwifery"), helping others find the truth through inquiry. He is famous for the statement "I know that I know nothing" and the principle "Know thyself." He explored questions of virtue, justice, piety, and knowledge. He criticized the Sophists for their false wisdom and exposed contradictions in their reasoning. Accused of corrupting the youth and impiety, he was sentenced to death and drank a cup of hemlock. His death became a symbol of fidelity to principles and the pursuit of truth. Socrates influenced Plato, Aristotle, and the entire course of Western philosophy. He remains a symbol of philosophical inquiry, irony, and moral integrity.

Фёдор Достоевский.name: Fyodor Dostoevsky
Фёдор Достоевский.description: Russian novelist, philosopher, and essayist, widely considered one of the greatest novelists in world literature. Born in Moscow into the family of a military doctor. He studied at the Engineering Academy in St. Petersburg but left the service for literature. He debuted with the novel "Poor Folk" (1846). In 1849, he was arrested for participating in the Petrashevsky Circle, sentenced to death, but pardoned at the last moment and exiled to katorga in Siberia (1850-1854), followed by military service. He returned to St. Petersburg in 1859. He wrote masterpiece novels: "Crime and Punishment" (1866), "The Idiot" (1868), "Demons" (1872), "The Adolescent" (1875), and "The Brothers Karamazov" (1880). He explored the depths of the human soul and problems of freedom, faith, suffering, good, and evil. He suffered from epilepsy, which was reflected in his work. He was a passionate gambler, often in debt. He traveled across Europe and criticized Western civilization. He died in St. Petersburg. Dostoevsky remains a master of psychological analysis, an explorer of the "underground" of the human psyche, and one of history's greatest philosopher-novelists.

Конфуций.name: Confucius
Конфуций.description: Chinese philosopher, teacher, and political figure whose teachings form the basis of Chinese civilization and culture. Born in Qufu, State of Lu (now Shandong Province), into an impoverished aristocratic family. He was orphaned early and raised by his mother. He received an education and worked as an official. He founded a private school, teaching students regardless of their background. He traveled across China offering his services to rulers but never held a high position. He returned to Lu, where he taught and edited classic texts. His teachings are recorded in the "Analects" (Lunyu), a collection of sayings compiled by his disciples. Confucius's philosophy is based on ethics, ritual (li), humaneness (ren), filial piety (xiao), and justice (yi). His doctrine of the "superior man" (junzi) represents the moral ideal. He emphasized the importance of education, self-improvement, and proper relationships within the family and society. He died in Qufu. Confucianism became the foundation of the Chinese state and culture for two millennia. Confucius remains a symbol of wisdom and moral excellence.

Махатма Ганди.name: Mahatma Gandhi
Махатма Ганди.description: Indian political and spiritual leader, founder of the philosophy of nonviolence (Satyagraha), and the Father of the Nation. Born in Porbandar, Gujarat, into the family of a local minister. At 19, he went to London to study law. He worked as a lawyer in South Africa (1893-1914), where he encountered racial discrimination and began the struggle for Indian rights. He developed the method of nonviolent resistance (Satyagraha). He returned to India in 1915 and became the leader of the independence movement. He organized massive campaigns: the boycott of British goods, the Salt March (1930), and the Quit India movement (1942). He conducted hunger strikes and spent time in prison. He preached simplicity, self-restraint, manual spinning (charkha), and Hindu-Muslim unity. In 1947, India gained independence but was partitioned into India and Pakistan. On January 30, 1948, he was assassinated by a Hindu fanatic in Delhi. Gandhi inspired civil rights movements worldwide, including that of Martin Luther King Jr. He remains a symbol of nonviolence, simplicity, and spiritual strength.

Николай Коперник.name: Nicolaus Copernicus
Николай Коперник.description: Polish astronomer, mathematician, canon, doctor, and economist, the architect of the heliocentric system of the world, which sparked a revolution in astronomy. Born in Toruń, Kingdom of Poland, into a merchant family. He was orphaned early and raised by his uncle, a bishop. He studied at Krakow University and later in Italy (Bologna, Padua, Ferrara), studying law, medicine, and astronomy. He earned a doctorate in canon law. Returning to Poland, he became a canon of the Warmia chapter, managing administrative affairs and treating the sick. In his spare time, he pursued astronomy, conducting observations and calculations. He developed the heliocentric model of the universe, where the Sun is at the center and Earth and other planets revolve around it. This contradicted the Ptolemaic geocentric system, which had been accepted for over 1,400 years. He published his seminal work, "De revolutionibus orbium coelestium" (On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres), in 1543, the year of his death, fearing persecution. The book was dedicated to Pope Paul III. Copernicus also worked in economics, formulating a law on money. His discovery laid the foundation for the Scientific Revolution and changed humanity's understanding of its place in the universe. Copernicus remains a symbol of scientific courage and the pursuit of truth.

Мария Склодовская-Кюри.name: Marie Curie
Мария Склодовская-Кюри.description: Polish-French physicist and chemist who conducted pioneering research on radioactivity. She was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize, the first person and the only woman to win the Nobel Prize twice, and the only person to win the Nobel Prize in two different scientific fields. Born Maria Salomea Skłodowska in Warsaw, in the Kingdom of Poland, she studied at the Flying University and began her practical scientific training in Warsaw. In 1891, she followed her elder sister Bronisława to study in Paris, where she earned her higher degrees and carried out her subsequent scientific work. In 1895, she married Pierre Curie, with whom she worked throughout her life. Together with her husband, she discovered polonium (named after Poland) and radium. In 1903, she shared the Nobel Prize in Physics with her husband and Henri Becquerel for their research on radiation. After her husband's death in 1906, she continued her work and became the first woman professor at the Sorbonne. In 1911, she won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for her discovery of radium and polonium and the isolation of radium. During World War I, she organized mobile X-ray units. She died of aplastic anemia caused by long-term radiation exposure. Curie remains a symbol of scientific perseverance, breaking gender barriers, and sacrifice for science.

Никола Тесла.name: Nikola Tesla
Никола Тесла.description: Serbian-American inventor, electrical engineer, mechanical engineer, and futurist, best known for his contributions to the design of the modern alternating current (AC) electricity supply system. Born in Smiljan, Austrian Empire (now Croatia), into the family of an Orthodox priest. He studied engineering in Graz and Prague. After working in Budapest and Paris, he emigrated to the United States in 1884. He worked for Thomas Edison but left due to disagreements. He established his own laboratory and developed the AC system, which triumphed over Edison's direct current (DC) in the "War of Currents." He invented the induction motor, transformers, and polyphase power transmission systems. He created the Tesla coil—a device to produce high-voltage, low-current, high-frequency alternating-current electricity. He experimented with wireless power transmission, radio, X-rays, and remote control. He built the Wardenclyffe Tower on Long Island for wireless energy transmission. He held over 300 patents and was a visionary who predicted many future technologies. He lived eccentrically, suffered from OCD, and adored pigeons. He died in poverty in New York. Tesla remains a symbol of genius, ingenuity, and vision.

Архимед.name: Archimedes
Архимед.description: Ancient Greek mathematician, physicist, engineer, inventor, and astronomer from Syracuse, regarded as one of the leading scientists in classical antiquity. Born in Syracuse, Sicily, to an astronomer father, he studied in Alexandria, the center of Hellenistic science. He returned to Syracuse to serve at the court of King Hiero II. He produced fundamental works in mathematics: he calculated pi with high precision, developed the method of exhaustion for calculating areas and volumes, and laid the foundations of integral calculus. He formulated Archimedes' principle concerning the buoyancy of bodies (the bathtub legend and "Eureka!"). He invented the Archimedean screw for raising water, and military machines like catapults and the "Claw of Archimedes." During the Roman siege of Syracuse (214-212 BC), he organized the defense with powerful defensive engines. He was killed by a Roman soldier during the fall of the city, despite orders to spare him. Archimedes successfully merged theoretical mathematics with practical engineering, laying the groundwork for many sciences. He remains the ultimate symbol of genius uniting theory and practice.

Елизавета II.name: Elizabeth II
Елизавета II.description: Queen of the United Kingdom and other Commonwealth realms from 1952 until her death in 2022. She was the longest-reigning British monarch in history, serving for 70 years. Born in London as Princess Elizabeth Alexandra Mary, she was the eldest daughter of the Duke of York (later King George VI). She did not expect to become queen, but after the abdication of her uncle Edward VIII in 1936, her father ascended to the throne. During World War II, she served in the Auxiliary Territorial Service. In 1947, she married Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh, and had four children. She became Queen at age 25 following her father's death. During her reign, she saw 15 Prime Ministers, from Churchill to Truss. She witnessed the decolonization of the British Empire, the Cold War, and the UK's entry into and exit from the EU. She made hundreds of state visits, becoming a symbol of stability and continuity. She celebrated Silver, Gold, Diamond, and Platinum Jubilees. She died at Balmoral Castle, Scotland. Elizabeth II remains a symbol of service, dignity, and the adaptation of the monarchy to the modern world.

Маргарет Тэтчер.name: Margaret Thatcher
Маргарет Тэтчер.description: British politician who served as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom from 1979 to 1990 and Leader of the Conservative Party from 1975 to 1990. She was the first female British Prime Minister and was known as the "Iron Lady." Born Margaret Hilda Roberts in Grantham, Lincolnshire, to a grocer and Methodist preacher. She graduated from Oxford University, studying chemistry and later law. She worked as a research chemist and then as a barrister. Elected to Parliament in 1959, she served as Secretary of State for Education (1970-1974) and Leader of the Opposition (1975-1979). As Prime Minister, she implemented radical economic reforms (Thatcherism): privatization of state-owned industries, lower taxes, curbs on trade unions, and deregulation of financial markets. She led the UK to victory in the Falklands War (1982) and was re-elected in 1983 and 1987. She was a key ally of Ronald Reagan during the Cold War. She resigned in 1990 following internal party divisions and was later granted a life peerage as Baroness Thatcher. She died in London. Thatcher transformed the British economy and politics, leaving a legacy of both revitalization and division.

Франклин Делано Рузвельт.name: Franklin D. Roosevelt
Франклин Делано Рузвельт.description: 32nd President of the United States (1933-1945), and the only president to be elected to four terms. He led the nation through the Great Depression and World War II. Born in Hyde Park, New York, into a wealthy, aristocratic family; he was a distant cousin of President Theodore Roosevelt. He graduated from Harvard and Columbia Law School. In 1910, he was elected to the New York State Senate, and from 1913 to 1920, he served as Assistant Secretary of the Navy. In 1921, he contracted polio, losing the use of his legs, but hid his disability from the public. Elected Governor of New York in 1928, he became President in 1932. He implemented the "New Deal"—a series of economic reforms aimed at recovery and relief. After the 1941 attack on Pearl Harbor, he led the US into World War II, working with Churchill and Stalin in the "Big Three." He articulated the "Four Freedoms": freedom of speech, freedom of worship, freedom from want, and freedom from fear. He died in April 1945, shortly before the war ended. Roosevelt restored American faith in democracy and government, remaining one of the nation's greatest presidents.

Генри Форд.name: Henry Ford
Генри Форд.description: American industrialist, business magnate, and founder of the Ford Motor Company, who revolutionized the automobile industry through the development of assembly line mass production. Born on a farm in Greenfield Township, Michigan, to Irish immigrants. He left home at 16 for Detroit to work as a machinist. In 1891, he became an engineer at the Edison Illuminating Company. In his spare time, he built his first automobile, the Quadricycle, in 1896. He founded the Ford Motor Company in 1903. In 1908, he introduced the Model T—a simple, reliable, and affordable car. In 1913, he implemented the assembly line, reducing chassis assembly time from 12 hours to 1.5 hours. In 1914, he introduced the 8-hour workday and a $5 daily wage—double the industry average. He produced millions of cars, making them accessible to the middle class. While he was a controversial figure, known for anti-Semitism and opposition to unions, he was also a philanthropist. He died in Dearborn, Michigan. Ford's legacy encompasses the creation of the mass-production era and a profound shift in global mobility and lifestyle.

Платон.name: Plato
Платон.description: Classical Greek philosopher, student of Socrates, teacher of Aristotle, and founder of the Academy in Athens—the first institution of higher learning in the Western world. Born into an aristocratic family in Athens, he received a broad education in music, gymnastics, and mathematics. At 20, he became a student of Socrates, under whose influence he turned to philosophy. After Socrates' death in 399 BC, he left Athens and traveled to Egypt, Italy, and Sicily. He returned in 387 BC and founded the Academy. He wrote in the form of dialogues, where Socrates often served as the main interlocutor. He developed the theory of Forms (or Ideas)—eternal, unchanging blueprints for things in the sensory world. He formulated a theory of knowledge suggesting the soul once inhabited the realm of Ideas, and learning is a process of recollection. In "The Republic," he described an ideal, just state ruled by philosopher-kings. His teachings profoundly influenced Western philosophy. He died in Athens. Plato remains one of history's greatest philosophers and the father of idealism.

Фридрих Ницше.name: Friedrich Nietzsche
Фридрих Ницше.description: German philosopher, poet, philologist, and composer whose work has exerted a profound influence on modern intellectual history. Born in Röcken, Prussia, into a pastor's family, he was orphaned early and raised by his mother and grandmother. He showed exceptional talent and became a professor of classical philology at the University of Basel at age 24. However, he left his academic career due to illness and disagreements with the scientific community. He lived a nomadic life in Italy, Switzerland, and France, in poverty and solitude. He developed a radical philosophy: he proclaimed the "death of God," criticized Christian morality as "slave morality," and developed concepts like "will to power," the "Übermensch" (Overman), and "eternal recurrence." He wrote in a poetic, aphoristic style, most notably in "Thus Spoke Zarathustra," "Beyond Good and Evil," and "On the Genealogy of Morals." He suffered from mental illness and spent the last 11 years of his life in a state of dementia. He died in Weimar. Nietzsche's influence on 20th-century philosophy, psychoanalysis, existentialism, and postmodernism is monumental. He remains a symbol of radical critique and creative freedom.
